event.title: Kenyan Cult Leader Paul Mackenzie Found Guilty of 191 Murders
event.canonical_title: Kenyan Cult Leader Paul Mackenzie Found Guilty of 191 Murders
event.summary: A Kenyan court has found Paul Mackenzie, a self-proclaimed preacher, and his associates responsible for the murders of 191 people, primarily children, linked to a starvation cult. The verdict was delivered on Monday, with Mackenzie having denied the charges, claiming he did not order the victims to starve in order to 'meet Jesus.'

timeline.summary: Paul Mackenzie, the leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect, has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult. The court found that he incited his followers to starve themselves and their families in a bid to 'meet Jesus.' Mackenzie and 28 accomplices were convicted for their roles in this tragic incident.

event_overview.title: About Kenya Cult Case
event_overview.subject: Kenya Cult Case
event_overview.summary: The Kenya cult case, commonly called the Shakahola case, concerns deaths and alleged abuse involving followers of Paul Nthenge Mackenzie’s Good News International Ministries in and around Shakahola Forest in Kilifi County on Kenya’s coast. It has produced several separate criminal proceedings arising from the same broader investigation, including murder, manslaughter, terrorism-related and child-protection allegations.

facts.label: Location and period
facts.value: The murder case concerned deaths in Shakahola Forest, Kilifi County, between January 2021 and September 2023.

facts.label: Organization
facts.value: Mackenzie led Good News International Ministries; Kenya’s Directorate of Criminal Investigations said the church was founded in 2010 and that the court found it operated as a cult.

facts.label: Discovery and investigation
facts.value: Authorities began uncovering mass graves in the Shakahola area in 2023; reporting based on the investigation has described more than 400 bodies being exhumed there.

facts.label: Murder case
facts.value: On October 19, 2026, the Mombasa High Court convicted Mackenzie and 28 co-accused on 191 murder counts involving 190 children and one adult; he was later sentenced to a total of 200 years’ imprisonment, subject to legal challenge or appeal.

facts.label: Separate proceedings
facts.value: The broader Shakahola investigation has involved distinct cases with different defendants, charges and alleged victim totals, including a 238-count manslaughter case against Mackenzie and 94 co-accused and terrorism-related proceedings.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers major 2026 court outcomes involving Mackenzie, especially the murder sentence and a later manslaughter ruling, but does not encompass the full Shakahola investigation, all co-accused, survivor issues, or every related criminal case.
